description: Research reviewed by Metzinger reports a high prevalence of asomatic out-of-body experiences and bodiless dreams in which body representation is reduced to an extensionless point while the sense of selfhood remains stable, many of them in lucid dreams.
limitations: A review of reports gathered by others, not a new study. Bodiless dreams are probably rare, and many reports come from lucid dreamers, a subset with possible biases.

sources.quote: recent research has demonstrated the high prevalence of asomatic OBEs and bodiless dreams in which the sense of selfhood remains stable
